subject: Newsletter mentions as company fields
to: Icypeas, co-founder or Head of Product
body:
Your homepage says the billion-plus record database is refreshed every month, and that 80% of your
customers embed the Icypeas API in their own product. Your scope is person and domain records, so
newsletter activity is a field you cannot fill today: which publications wrote about a company, in
what context, and on what date.

NewsletterFIT indexes 26,401 public newsletter publications and 141,392 articles, with company,
people, topic, guest and sponsor extraction, each carrying the article URL and date.

If that is a field your customers would pay for, I can send 1,000 enriched domains as a sample. If
your road map already covers it, telling me that is just as useful.

subject: A newsletter corpus for your fund customers
meta: 2. KADOA   66/100  gap confirmed  contact: support@kadoa.com, or max@kadoa.com unverified
body:
Your docs describe a workflow's source as the set of URLs it extracts from, with HTML, XML, RSS, JSON
and PDF supported. That means a fund wanting newsletter coverage has to hand-build per-publication
pipelines, one site at a time.

NewsletterFIT already holds 26,401 public newsletter publications and 141,392 articles, with
companies, people, topics, guests and 2,218 sponsors extracted, and the article URL and date on every
record. It could land as a licensed input beside your own collection rather than something you build.

Would a sample of 5,000 recent items for a sector you serve be useful? If you already ingest
newsletters, say so and I will stop there.

subject: Company-side newsletter signals beside your candidate data
to: HireEZ, VP Product or Head of Data Partnerships
meta: 3. HIREEZ   47/100  gap confirmed but adjacent  contact: sales form only
body:
Your sourcing is described as ATS, job boards and the open web, and your blog puts the open-web
figure at over a billion professional profiles. Newsletter coverage is outside that, and it points at
companies rather than candidates: which publications wrote about a hiring brand, and who sponsors
them.

NewsletterFIT holds 26,401 publications and 141,392 articles with company, people, topic and sponsor
extraction, each with source URL and date. It would sit beside your candidate data, not replace it,
and I am not going to pretend we have resumes.

If a company-level signal is useful to your product team, I can send a sample. If not, one line
saying so closes it.

subject: A ready newsletter corpus instead of a collection project
to: Zyte, Head of Data Acquisition or VP Product, Zyte Data
meta: 4. ZYTE   45/100  gap unverified  contact: Talk to us form
body:
Zyte API already auto-extracts article content from any URL, so the question for a newsletter corpus
is not whether it can be scraped but whether it is worth building and maintaining 26,000 publication
pipelines.

We have done that part: 26,401 public newsletter publications, 141,392 articles, with company,
people, topic, guest and sponsor extraction and the article URL and date on each record. If your
managed data team wants to offer newsletter coverage to customers, licensing ours is faster than
collecting it.

Happy to send a sample and a coverage summary. If it duplicates work you already run, tell me and
that answer is useful too.

subject: Newsletter text as a text source
to: Orbifold AI, Head of Data Partnerships
meta: 5. ORBIFOLD AI   26/100  gap unverified, wrong domain  contact: chat@orbifold.ai
body:
Your site describes turning enterprise documents and email into schema-mapped, timestamped datasets
for training and retrieval. Public newsletter issues are long-form business text with named companies
in them, which is the same shape of input, sourced from outside a customer's own estate.

NewsletterFIT holds 26,401 publications and 141,392 articles, with entity, topic and sponsor
extraction, each record with URL and date. If a customer-facing dataset of that kind is useful, I can
send a sample. If your roadmap is entirely customer-tenant data, a one-line no is fine and I will not
follow up.

subject: Newsletter topic activity for the Co-op
to: Ryan Klekas, VP Partner Development, Bombora
meta: 8. BOMBORA   53/100  gap unverified, supply-side  contact: no public email, buyer Ryan Klekas
body:
Bombora's Co-op is described as thousands of media destinations including publishers, B2B brands and
premium data providers, and topic-level research behaviour is modelled from that. Newsletters are
publishers whose behaviour may already reach you through their web archives, or may not reach you at
all, and I would rather ask than guess.

NewsletterFIT holds 26,401 publications and 141,392 articles, with companies, people, topics, guests
and 2,218 sponsors extracted, plus repeated snapshots of publication activity. If a newsletter
source adds topic coverage your web signals miss, a licensing conversation is the right shape. If it
does not, that answer is worth having.

subject: Newsletter topic activity as an intent input

body:
6sense's documented inputs are research and review-site intent, web deanonymisation and first-party
engagement, complemented by partners including Bombora, TechTarget, TrustRadius and G2. I could not

NewsletterFIT holds 26,401 publications and 141,392 articles with company, topic, guest and sponsor
